The nondegenerate Hopf theorem gives the stable small cycle and physical amplitude. At a=0 the cubic radial damping is strict, and stable foliation transfers the t-weighted center decay to all local trajectories outside the one-dimensional strong stable manifold. No numerical integration is treated as an infinite-time proof.

value.rationale: Sprott case F is an established minimal quadratic chaos benchmark. Its author published a two-parameter phase-region diagram but without analytic Hopf criticality across the entire positive-damping axis. The exact sign-definite rational first Lyapunov coefficient proves there is no Bautin reversal on the entire natural Hopf boundary, fixes the small-cycle amplitude for quantitative bifurcation work, and gives an explicit inverse-time decay constant precisely where linear stability is inconclusive. This goes beyond routine equilibrium checking and is motivated by resolving that mathematical transition, rather than an arbitrary slice.
